prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Meridian Regional Air Traffic Flow Management and Airport Collaborative Decision-Making System = Regional Flow Platform (Cedarbell). Airports Meridian International, Harbor East, North Valley, Lakeside Regional, Southport keep safety authority. TOBT (Target Off Block Time): issued only if capacity/ground path allow; frozen at horizon unless exception recorded; revised only on turnaround-actor confirmation. Parts: Demand Prediction Service (Marlinstone; Flight Intent Message incl. amended for diversions vs Airport Capacity Plan, AAR=Airport Acceptance Rate); Capacity Assessment Module (CAM; AAR per runway config; checks runway/stand/sector/handling/service before diversion recommendation); Slot Allocation Engine (Blueharbor; CTT=Calculated Takeoff Time; Ground Delay Program; Pushback Window Token); Departure Metering Service (Emberline; TOBT protecting CTT; CTT to TSM); North/South Runway Meters; Surface Surveillance Adapter (status to Ramp Movement Board, TSM); East/West Apron Sensors; Airport CDM Portal (Foxglove; Common Situation Display; Pushback Window Token protects diversion-recovery departures); Tower Sequence Manager (TSM, Ironleaf); Gate Conflict Detector (Gate Reopening Memo; flags diversion parking vs turnaround/critical departure bank conflicts); Airline Interface Adapter (Late Baggage Tag List to Ground Handling Dispatcher); Handling Resource Planner; Alert Distribution Hub (Lantern; role-specific alert summaries; MUST distribute surface advisories within latency); Ramp Movement Board (Skylark; Fuel Truck Hold Advice; MUST refresh apron layer within 5 s); Collaborative Decision Log; Audit Event Ledger (MUST record adjustments, rationale, actor, timestamp, overrides; with Identity Access Service traces who viewed/changed/approved); Sector Load Monitor (Departure Fix Load Sheet); Business Rules Registry; Performance Analytics Warehouse (actuals vs diversion plan, post-ops review); Time Synchronization Service; Arrival Regulation Console (Nightjar); Integrated Tactical Management Position; Weather Ingest Gateway (Orchard); Digital Briefing Room (records rationale, priority, resources, recovery target to Decision Log). Actors: Airport Duty Manager (Medical Diversion Notice), Tower Supervisor, Airspace Sector Planner (Tactical Regulation Proposal), Emergency Response Coordinator, Aircraft Operator Representative, Regional Flow Manager, Network Operations Liaison (network effects), Slot Coordinator (Slot Compliance State), Data Governance Steward (role restriction), Airline Operations Coordinator (passenger/crew/maintenance/rotation impacts), Ground Handling Dispatcher and Ramp Control Lead (confirm stand/towing/fuel/unloading

New part:
S521: The Airline Operations Coordinator confirms whether the aircraft can remain on plan, accept a short readiness deferral, or require a revised departure intent.
S522: The Handling Resource Planner assigns a severity level to the handler exception and suppresses duplicate updates while the accountable party is still working the same recovery action.
S523: The Ground Handling Dispatcher sends the Towbar Shortage Report when towbar availability cannot support the agreed pushback sequence.
S524: Towbar availability is escalated only when the missing equipment affects a flight inside the active departure planning horizon or blocks a higher-priority aircraft movement.
S525: The Ramp Movement Board displays the resulting constraint as a stand-level exception with a time band rather than as a continuous stream of equipment messages.
S526: Handler exceptions include staffing gaps, equipment unserviceability, access limitations, and service sequencing conflicts that could invalidate a readiness milestone.
S527: The Airport CDM Portal keeps detailed handler notes available to authorized users while the Common Situation Display shows only the flight impact, severity, and expected recovery window.
S528: This separation prevents local troubleshooting details from crowding the regional view used by the Regional Flow Manager, Tower Supervisor, and Slot Coordinator.
S529: The Alert Distribution Hub routes notifications according to severity, time to milestone, and subscribed operational role, rather than broadcasting every exception to all users.
S530: A baggage or handler exception becomes a coordination issue when it threatens the Target Off Block Time, the Calculated Takeoff Time, or an agreed runway metering sequence.
S531: At that point, the Airport CDM Portal prompts the accountable role to record the proposed mitigation in the Collaborative Decision Log.
S532: The Regional Flow Manager sees aggregated impact by departure bank, runway stream, and airline group instead of individual baggage or handler work items.
S533: The Slot Allocation Engine uses the sanitized readiness state when evaluating whether a regulated flight can keep its allocated departure opportunity.
S534: The Departure Metering Service applies exception status only after the Business Rules Registry threshold confirms that the condition is operationally material.
S535: Nightjar shall suppress handler-exception annotations for arriving flights unless the exception changes the Airport Acceptance Rate or a regulated arrival sequence.
S536: The Tower Sequence Manager receives a stable readiness indicator and an escalation flag, which allows tower planning to continue without interpreting ramp work details.
S537: The Audit Event Ledger records who raised, changed, acknowledged, or closed each escalated exception so that later review can distinguish data noise from operational decisions.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
